commentEn: Apple Intelligence launches, AI game NPCs achieve natural dialogue, Chinese AI chips exported to Europe—AI is moving from the lab to the consumer market, and from the domestic market to global competition.

newsItems.titleEn: Apple Intelligence Officially Launches, Deeply Integrating Siri and System Apps
newsItems.summaryEn: Apple has officially launched Apple Intelligence in iOS 18.1, deeply integrating it with core system apps such as Siri, Mail, Messages, and Photos. Apple Intelligence understands user intent, automatically generates text and images, summarizes emails and messages, and intelligently organizes photos. Apple CEO Tim Cook stated that Apple Intelligence will redefine the personal assistant and deliver a truly useful AI experience to users.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Game NPCs Achieve Truly Natural Dialogue, Revolutionizing Player Experience
newsItems.summaryEn: Game developer Ubisoft has unveiled AI-driven NPC technology that enables characters to engage in truly natural conversations with players. These NPCs can understand context, recall past interactions, and dynamically adjust dialogue strategies based on player behavior. Tests show the AI NPCs achieved a dialogue naturalness score of 90, significantly outperforming traditional scripted NPCs. Ubisoft announced that the technology will be deployed at scale in its new 2027 game releases, delivering highly immersive gaming experiences.

newsItems.titleEn: China's AI Chips Make First Export to Europe: Homegrown Alternatives Step onto the Global Stage
newsItems.summaryEn: Chinese AI chipmaker Cambricon announced the first-ever European export of its MLU370 chip, securing an order from a German automaker. This milestone marks the debut of Chinese AI chips in the European market, signaling a major breakthrough in the technological capabilities and global recognition of domestic AI chips. According to Cambricon, the MLU370 matches international advanced standards in performance and power efficiency, and will be deployed in autonomous driving and smart cockpit applications.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Enterprise with On-Premises Deployment
newsItems.summaryEn: OpenAI has officially launched ChatGPT Enterprise, supporting deployment in private cloud or on-premises environments to ensure data security and compliance. Offering enhanced performance, greater customization, and stricter security controls, ChatGPT Enterprise is ideal for sectors with stringent data security requirements, such as finance, healthcare, and government. OpenAI reports that over 100 enterprise customers have already signed up, including several Fortune 500 companies.

newsItems.titleEn: Global AI Talent Gap Reaches 4 Million; Talent Development Becomes Industry Bottleneck
newsItems.summaryEn: LinkedIn has released a report revealing that the global AI talent shortage has reached 4 million, with the most acute shortages in large models, AI chips, and AI security. The report attributes this supply-demand gap primarily to rapidly evolving skill requirements driven by fast-paced AI advancements, university AI curricula lagging behind industry demands, and top AI talent being monopolized by leading companies. Experts recommend that universities strengthen their AI academic programs while companies increase investment in internal training.

titleEn: AI News | Anthropic Raises $5 Billion, AI Legal Assistant Approved, Meta Launches AI Translation Model
summaryEn: Anthropic has raised $5 billion, reaching a valuation of $180 billion. The American Bar Association has approved the first AI legal assistant for drafting legal documents. Meta released a borderless translation model supporting real-time translation across 100 languages. NVIDIA unveiled the DGX B200 AI supercomputer, delivering a threefold performance boost. Meanwhile, Chinese AI unicorn Moonshot AI has surpassed a $5 billion valuation. AI adoption is accelerating across the finance, legal, and translation sectors.
commentEn: Anthropic raises $5B, an AI legal assistant gains approval, and Meta open-sources a translation model—AI is shifting from a tech race to commercial deployment, expanding from the English-speaking world to global applications.

newsItems.titleEn: Anthropic Raises $5 Billion at $180 Billion Valuation
newsItems.summaryEn: AI safety company Anthropic has closed a $5 billion Series D funding round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with follow-on investments from Google, Spark Capital, and others. This brings Anthropic's valuation to $180 billion, making it one of the highest-valued AI startups globally. The company stated that the funds will be used to build out computing infrastructure, advance frontier research, and recruit top talent, accelerating the iteration of the Claude model series.

newsItems.titleEn: American Bar Association Approves First AI Legal Assistant to Help Draft Legal Documents
newsItems.summaryEn: The American Bar Association (ABA) has officially approved the AI legal assistant LexAI for drafting legal documents and conducting legal research. LexAI can comprehend complex legal cases and generate documents such as contracts, pleadings, and legal opinions, achieving an accuracy rate of over 95%. The ABA stated that while AI legal assistants will significantly boost attorney productivity and reduce legal costs, lawyers must still review and assume full responsibility for all AI-generated content.

newsItems.titleEn: Meta Unveils Borderless Translation Model with Real-Time Support for 100 Languages
newsItems.summaryEn: Meta AI Research has launched the No Borders translation model, enabling real-time translation across 100 languages, including numerous low-resource languages. The model delivers exceptional accuracy and fluency, excelling in complex scenarios involving dialects, colloquialisms, and specialized terminology. Meta announced that No Borders will be open-sourced to empower developers worldwide in building multilingual applications and fostering cross-cultural communication.

newsItems.titleEn: NVIDIA Launches DGX B200 AI Supercomputer with 3x Performance Boost
newsItems.summaryEn: NVIDIA has unveiled its next-generation AI supercomputer, the DGX B200, featuring eight Blackwell Ultra GPUs. It delivers 3x the AI training performance and 2.5x the energy efficiency of the previous-generation DGX H100. Capable of training trillion-parameter models, the DGX B200 is ideal for complex AI tasks such as large language and multimodal models. According to NVIDIA, the system will help enterprises and research institutions accelerate AI innovation and deployment.

titleEn: AI News | OpenAI Acquires Jewish, Copyright Disputes Over AI-Generated Music, China's Registered Large Models Top 150
summaryEn: OpenAI acquires AI startup Jewish for $2 billion to bolster its search and reasoning capabilities; AI music generation sparks copyright disputes as multiple record labels sue AI companies; the number of registered large models in China surpasses 150, signaling an increasingly mature industry ecosystem; Amazon launches Rufus, an AI shopping assistant, to enhance the shopping experience; and global AI investment hits a record high of $100 billion in the first three quarters. AI is rapidly penetrating the search, music, and e-commerce sectors.
commentEn: OpenAI acquires Jewish to bolster search, AI music sparks copyright disputes, and China's registered large models surpass 150—as the AI industry expands rapidly, it also faces mounting challenges in copyright, regulation, and commercialization.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI Acquires AI Startup Jewish for $2 Billion to Enhance Search and Reasoning Capabilities
newsItems.summaryEn: OpenAI has announced the acquisition of Jewish, an AI startup specializing in AI search and reasoning, for $2 billion. Its search engine can comprehend complex queries and deliver accurate, in-depth answers. This acquisition will bolster OpenAI's search capabilities, positioning it in direct competition with Google. OpenAI stated that Jewish's technology will be integrated into ChatGPT to enhance its information retrieval and reasoning capabilities.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Music Generation Sparks Copyright Controversy: Multiple Record Labels Sue AI Firms
newsItems.summaryEn: Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, and other major record labels have jointly sued AI music generation companies Suno and Udio for copyright infringement. The labels allege that the AI models were trained on vast amounts of copyrighted music, resulting in generated tracks that are highly similar to the original works. This lawsuit is set to become a landmark case in determining the copyright status of AI-generated content, with profound implications for AI music, AI art, and related fields.

newsItems.titleEn: China's Registered Large Models Surpass 150 as Industry Ecosystem Matures
newsItems.summaryEn: According to the Cyberspace Administration of China, the number of registered large models in the country has surpassed 150, spanning general-purpose, industry-specific, and vertical categories. These registered models have cumulatively served over 500 million users, with daily API calls exceeding 5 billion. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology notes that China's large model industry has shifted from technological exploration to large-scale application, generating a range of exemplary use cases across finance, healthcare, education, and manufacturing.

newsItems.titleEn: Amazon Launches AI Shopping Assistant Rufus to Enhance Shopping Experience
newsItems.summaryEn: Amazon has officially launched Rufus, an AI shopping assistant that helps users discover products, compare items, and get shopping advice through natural language conversations. Rufus can understand complex queries, such as "birthday gifts for a 5-year-old," and recommend relevant products. Amazon says Rufus will be integrated into the Amazon App to help users find exactly what they want faster and enhance the overall shopping experience.

newsItems.titleEn: Global AI Investment Hits Record $100 Billion in First Three Quarters
newsItems.summaryEn: Market research firm CB Insights reports that global AI investment reached a record high of $100 billion in the first three quarters of 2026, surging 60% year-on-year. Large models, AI chips, and AI applications emerged as the primary investment hotspots, accounting for over 70% of the total. The report notes that AI investment is shifting from early-stage technological exploration to commercial applications, with investors increasingly favoring AI companies with clear business models and revenue streams.

titleEn: AI News | Google Launches Gemini 2.0, Huawei Ascend 910C Enters Mass Production, AI Education Platform Surpasses 100 Million Users
summaryEn: Google launches the Gemini 2.0 series with significantly enhanced multimodal capabilities. Huawei's Ascend 910C AI chip officially enters mass production, matching NVIDIA A100 performance. Global AI education platforms surpass 100 million users, making personalized learning a reality. Microsoft Teams integrates an AI meeting assistant to automatically record and summarize meetings. China's AI unicorn count tops 500 as the industry ecosystem grows increasingly robust. Overall, AI is driving major strides across education, workplace productivity, and chip development.
commentEn: The multimodal upgrade to Gemini 2.0, mass production of the Ascend 910C, and the widespread adoption of AI education—AI is transitioning from technological breakthroughs to real-world applications, evolving from an elite tool into ubiquitous infrastructure.

newsItems.titleEn: Google Launches Gemini 2.0 Series: Fully Upgraded Multimodal Capabilities and 1 Million Token Context Support
newsItems.summaryEn: At the Cloud Next conference, Google unveiled the Gemini 2.0 model family, featuring three versions: Flash, Pro, and Ultra. The new models excel in multimodal understanding, long-context handling, and code generation, supporting a context window of up to 1 million tokens. Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced that Gemini 2.0 will be deeply integrated into products such as Google Workspace and Android, serving as the cornerstone of Google's AI strategy.

newsItems.titleEn: Huawei Ascend 910C AI Chip Enters Mass Production, Performance Rivals Nvidia A100
newsItems.summaryEn: Huawei has announced that its Ascend 910C AI chip has officially entered mass production, delivering 90% of the performance of NVIDIA's A100 while cutting power consumption by 20%. Built on SMIC's 7nm process, the Ascend 910C is currently China's most powerful AI training chip. Huawei stated that the chip will be prioritized for domestic cloud providers and AI companies, with orders already exceeding 100,000 units, marking a major breakthrough for domestic AI chips in the high-end market.

newsItems.titleEn: Global AI Education Platform Surpasses 100 Million Users as Personalized Learning Becomes a Reality
newsItems.summaryEn: Market research shows that the global user base for AI education platforms has surpassed 100 million, with Chinese users accounting for over 30%. These platforms deliver fully personalized learning paths and content tailored to students' individual pace, knowledge mastery, and learning styles. Data indicates that students using AI education platforms experience a 40% boost in learning efficiency and a 35% improvement in knowledge retention. AI is fundamentally reshaping teaching methods across the education sector.

newsItems.titleEn: Microsoft Teams Integrates AI Meeting Assistant to Automatically Record and Summarize Meetings
newsItems.summaryEn: Microsoft has announced the integration of an AI meeting assistant into Teams, featuring automatic recording, speaker identification, key information extraction, and meeting minutes generation. The assistant also supports real-time multilingual translation to enable seamless communication for global teams. According to Microsoft, this feature will boost meeting efficiency by 50% and significantly reduce post-meeting administrative time. It will be available to enterprise users in November 2026.

titleEn: AI News | Tesla Optimus Gen-3 Unveiled, Alibaba Cloud's Qwen Open-Sourced, AI Medical Diagnosis Approved
summaryEn: Tesla unveiled the Optimus Gen-3 humanoid robot, featuring smooth locomotion and precise manipulation; Alibaba Cloud open-sourced the Qwen-72B model, delivering performance on par with GPT-4; the FDA approved the first AI-powered early cancer detection system, achieving 95% accuracy; ByteDance launched Doubao 2.0, emphasizing multimodal capabilities and cost-effectiveness; and the global AI chip market surpassed $50 billion, with Nvidia's market share dipping to 60%. These developments mark significant breakthroughs for AI across hardware, open-source, and healthcare.
commentEn: Optimus Gen-3 brings robots into the home, open-sourcing Qwen drives ecosystem growth, and AI medical diagnostics save lives—AI is moving from the digital realm to the physical world, evolving from a tool into foundational infrastructure.

newsItems.titleEn: Tesla Unveils Optimus Gen-3: Smooth Walking, Precise Manipulation, Mass Production Imminent
newsItems.summaryEn: At Tesla AI Day, the Optimus Gen-3 humanoid robot was unveiled, showcasing fluid walking, precise hand manipulation, and intelligent environmental awareness. The next-generation Optimus can handle household chores such as folding clothes, tidying rooms, and basic cooking. Elon Musk announced that Optimus Gen-3 will enter mass production in 2027 with an initial price of around $20,000, aiming to become a general-purpose robot for households and the service industry.

newsItems.titleEn: Alibaba Cloud Open-Sources Tongyi Qianwen 72B Model, Performance Rivals GPT-4
newsItems.summaryEn: At the Apsara Conference, Alibaba Cloud announced the official open-source release of its 72-billion-parameter Tongyi Qianwen model, which delivers GPT-4-level performance across multiple benchmarks. Bilingual in Chinese and English, the model excels in code generation, mathematical reasoning, and Chinese comprehension. Alibaba Cloud stated that this open-source initiative aims to drive the growth of China's AI ecosystem, noting that over 100,000 developers have already built applications using Tongyi Qianwen.

newsItems.titleEn: FDA Approves First AI-Driven Early Cancer Detection System, Achieving 95% Accuracy
newsItems.summaryEn: The U.S. FDA has approved an AI cancer diagnostic system developed by PathAI that can detect multiple cancers early through blood tests with 95% accuracy. As the first AI cancer screening tool to receive full FDA approval, it is expected to significantly reduce early diagnosis costs. PathAI's CEO stated that the system will be widely deployed across U.S. hospitals in 2027, potentially saving millions of lives.

newsItems.titleEn: ByteDance Unveils Doubao 2.0 LLM, Highlighting Multimodality and Low Cost
newsItems.summaryEn: ByteDance has officially launched version 2.0 of its Doubao large model, showcasing outstanding multimodal understanding and generation capabilities across text, images, video, and audio. Priced at just one-third the cost of GPT-4's API, Doubao 2.0 significantly lowers the barrier to enterprise adoption. ByteDance reports that the Doubao model is now integrated into products such as Douyin and Toutiao, handling over 5 billion API calls daily.

newsItems.titleEn: Global AI Chip Market Tops $50 Billion Amid Shifting Competitive Landscape
newsItems.summaryEn: Market research firm Gartner reports that the global AI chip market will surpass $50 billion in 2026, up 45% year-on-year. NVIDIA's market share is projected to drop from 85% to 60%, while AMD, Intel, and Chinese vendors see significant gains. The report notes that the AI chip market is shifting from NVIDIA's sole dominance to a more diversified competitive landscape, with custom and edge AI chips emerging as new growth drivers.

titleEn: AI News | Microsoft Copilot Workspace Launches, Baidu ERNIE Bot 4.5 Goes Live, AI Coding Assistant Market Surges
summaryEn: Microsoft launches Copilot Workspace, enabling end-to-end AI assistance from requirements to code; Baidu officially launches ERNIE Bot 4.5 with significantly enhanced multimodal capabilities; the AI coding assistant market enters a phase of explosive growth as GitHub Copilot surpasses 50 million users; Apple acquires AI startup IQM to accelerate Siri's AI transformation; and the number of registered AI foundation models in China exceeds 100, marking a maturing industry ecosystem. AI is evolving from a tool into a platform.
commentEn: From Copilot Workspace to ERNIE Bot 4.5, AI is evolving from point solutions to end-to-end platforms. The booming coding assistant market suggests that AI's first major disruption may well be the workflows of knowledge workers.

newsItems.titleEn: Microsoft Launches Copilot Workspace: End-to-End AI-Assisted Development from Requirements to Code
newsItems.summaryEn: At the Ignite conference, Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspace, a revolutionary AI development environment that generates complete applications directly from natural language requirements. Developers simply describe their requirements, and Copilot Workspace automatically plans the architecture, generates code, creates tests, and deploys the application. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated that this will boost software development efficiency tenfold, empowering everyone to become a developer.

newsItems.titleEn: Baidu Officially Launches ERNIE Bot 4.5 with Significantly Enhanced Multimodal Capabilities
newsItems.summaryEn: Baidu has officially launched ERNIE Bot 4.5, achieving major breakthroughs in multimodal understanding, long-context processing, and logical reasoning. The new version supports multiple input formats, including images, videos, and audio, and can comprehend complex charts and data visualizations. Baidu CEO Robin Li announced that daily API calls for ERNIE Bot 4.5 have surpassed 1 billion, making it one of the most active AI applications in China.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Coding Assistant Market Explodes: GitHub Copilot Surpasses 50 Million Users
newsItems.summaryEn: GitHub announced that Copilot's paid subscriber base has surpassed 50 million, with monthly active developers exceeding 100 million. Data shows that developers using Copilot have achieved a 55% increase in code output and a 30% reduction in bug rates. The AI coding assistant market has consolidated into a triad led by GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Codeium, with the market size projected to reach $10 billion by 2027.

newsItems.titleEn: Apple Acquires AI Startup IQM to Accelerate Siri's AI Overhaul
newsItems.summaryEn: Apple has acquired Finnish AI startup IQM for approximately $1 billion, a company specializing in the integration of quantum computing and AI. This acquisition will help Apple accelerate Siri's AI upgrade, enhancing its capabilities in complex conversations, reasoning, and task execution. Analysts view this as a major strategic move in the AI race, aimed at closing the gap with OpenAI and Google.

titleEn: AI News | Claude Opus 4.9 Released, NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra Enters Mass Production, China's AI Chips Break 7nm Barrier
summaryEn: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 4.9, boosting reasoning capabilities by 40% and cutting costs by 25%. NVIDIA officially begins mass production of its Blackwell Ultra chips, delivering 2.5 times the performance of the previous generation. A Chinese AI chip firm successfully breaks through the 7nm process, further advancing domestic substitution. OpenAI announces GPT-6 will support a million-token context window. Implementation rules for the EU AI Act are now in place, as the global regulatory framework gradually takes shape. The AI industry is advancing in parallel across three dimensions: compute, models, and regulation.
commentEn: Performance upgrades to Claude Opus 4.9, the mass production of Blackwell Ultra, and China's 7nm chip breakthroughs highlight the AI industry's simultaneous advances in computing power, models, and process technology. Meanwhile, the rollout of the EU regulatory framework reminds us that technological progress must go hand in hand with institutional development.

newsItems.titleEn: Anthropic Launches Claude Opus 4.9: Reasoning Capabilities Up 40%, Costs Down 25%
newsItems.summaryEn: Anthropic has officially launched the Claude Opus 4.9 model, delivering significant improvements in complex reasoning, code generation, and multi-step task planning. Compared to Opus 4.8, the new model boosts reasoning capabilities by 40%, reduces API costs by 25%, and expands the context window to 500K tokens. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated that Opus 4.9 greatly enhances practical utility while maintaining robust safety, making it ideal for complex enterprise applications.

newsItems.titleEn: NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra Chips Enter Mass Production, Delivering 2.5x Performance Boost Over Previous Generation
newsItems.summaryEn: NVIDIA announced that its Blackwell Ultra AI chips have officially entered mass production, with the first batch supplying top cloud providers including Microsoft, Google, and Amazon. Built on TSMC's 4NP process and packing 208 billion transistors, the Blackwell Ultra delivers 2.5x the AI training performance and 3x the inference efficiency of the previous-generation Hopper. Jensen Huang stated that the Blackwell Ultra will usher in a new era of AI, shifting the industry focus from training to inference.

newsItems.titleEn: Chinese AI Chip Company Achieves 7nm Process Breakthrough, Advancing Domestic Substitution
newsItems.summaryEn: A leading domestic AI chipmaker has announced the successful mass production of a 7nm AI inference chip, delivering 80% of the performance of Nvidia's A100 while reducing power consumption by 30%. This marks China's first large-scale production of advanced-node AI chips, signifying major breakthroughs in both the technological capabilities and production capacity of domestic AI chips. The chip will be initially supplied to domestic cloud service providers and AI companies, accelerating the process of domestic substitution.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI Announces GPT-6 to Support Million-Token Context, Slated for 2027 Release
newsItems.summaryEn: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman revealed on social media that the next-generation model, GPT-6, will feature a massive 1 million-token context window and is slated for release in Q1 2027. GPT-6 will adopt a novel Mixture of Experts architecture, significantly reducing training costs while maintaining performance. Altman stated that GPT-6 aims to achieve true artificial general intelligence, capable of understanding and processing the vast majority of human knowledge domains.

newsItems.titleEn: EU AI Act Implementing Rules Officially Released, Global Regulatory Framework Taking Shape
newsItems.summaryEn: The European Commission has officially published the implementing rules for the Artificial Intelligence Act, outlining compliance requirements and review procedures for high-risk AI systems. Under these rules, all AI systems operating in the EU must undergo risk assessments, with high-risk applications in sectors such as healthcare, finance, and law enforcement requiring prior authorization. As the world's first comprehensive AI regulatory framework, it will profoundly impact the global AI industry and has already sparked debate over balancing innovation with regulation.

titleEn: AI News | AI Breaks Video Turing Test, Meta Open-Sources AI Peripherals, arXiv Throttles AI Papers
summaryEn: AI video generation shatters the "Video Turing Test," drawing 17 million online viewers; Meta open-sources Muse Gadgets, empowering developers to build custom AI peripherals; arXiv imposes its strictest rate limits amid a surge in AI paper submissions; China's open-source decision model StartLux tops the leaderboard; and the mass production of AI-powered "pig-butchering" scams raises concerns. AI is reshaping content creation, the hardware development ecosystem, and academic publishing.
commentEn: AI video shatters the Turing test, Meta opens its hardware ecosystem, and arXiv is forced to rate-limit submissions—as the boundaries of AI capabilities continue to expand, content authenticity, academic integrity, and fraud awareness all face unprecedented challenges.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Shatters the "Video Turing Test," Drawing 17 Million Online Viewers
newsItems.summaryEn: AI video generation technology has achieved a milestone breakthrough by successfully passing the "Video Turing Test," drawing 17 million online viewers. This signifies that AI's capabilities in visual content generation have advanced to the point of being virtually indistinguishable from real video, carrying profound implications for content creation, film and television production, and the governance of misinformation.

newsItems.titleEn: Meta Open-Sources Muse Gadgets, Enabling Developers Worldwide to Build Their Own AI Peripherals
newsItems.summaryEn: Meta has officially open-sourced the Muse Gadgets project, empowering developers worldwide to independently design and manufacture AI peripherals. This initiative lowers the barrier to entry for AI hardware development and fosters a diverse AI peripheral ecosystem, paving the way for a wide array of new form factors, ranging from earbuds to smart rings.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Sparks Paper Explosion: arXiv Imposes Strictest Rate Limits
newsItems.summaryEn: The surge in AI-generated papers is pushing the academic peer-review system to the brink of collapse, prompting the arXiv preprint server to implement its strictest rate-limiting measures yet. While AI has lowered the barrier to writing research papers, it has also resulted in highly inconsistent quality, driving the academic community to seek a new balance.

newsItems.titleEn: China's Open-Source Decision Model StartLux Surges to Global No. 1
newsItems.summaryEn: China's open-source project StartLux has topped international benchmarks with its decision-making model, dethroning the previous leader, the Jev model. This marks a significant breakthrough for China in AI decision-making capabilities, underscoring the growing competitiveness of its open-source ecosystem.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Mass-Produces Pig-Butchering Scams as Fraud Scales Up
newsItems.summaryEn: Criminals are leveraging AI to mass-produce "pig-butchering" scams, deploying end-to-end AI across the entire chain from script generation to voice cloning. AI has lowered the barrier to fraud, making scams more convincing and harder to detect, underscoring the need for public vigilance.

titleEn: AI News | OpenAI Unveils GPT-6.1 Sol, Broadcom Secures 60B Funding, DeepSeek Open-Sources Ascend Components
summaryEn: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol, offering near-Astra performance at just one-fifth the cost; Broadcom raises $60 billion to fund Anthropic's chip project; DeepSeek open-sources Huawei Ascend foundational components, adding a powerful new tool to the domestic AI ecosystem; Anthropic's red team tests on GLM-5.3 reveal its safety guardrails are virtually non-existent; and Toshiba plans to double HDD production capacity for AI data centers. AI competition is now expanding beyond model performance into infrastructure and security.
commentEn: GPT-6.1 Sol prioritizes cost-effectiveness, Broadcom bets 60 billion on Anthropic chips, and DeepSeek bridges the domestic compute gap—AI competition is shifting from model performance to a dual contest over infrastructure and security.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Sol: Performance Nears Astra at Just One-Fifth the Price
newsItems.summaryEn: OpenAI has launched GPT-6.1 Sol, designed to handle tasks ranging from professional office workflows and computer control to agentic coding. It delivers performance approaching that of the flagship Astra at just one-fifth the price, offering a substantial boost in cost-effectiveness. Following the controversy over Astra's failure to pass safety reviews, the release of 6.1 Sol demonstrates OpenAI's effort to strike a balance between performance and safety.

newsItems.titleEn: Broadcom Raises $60 Billion to Fund Anthropic Chip Project
newsItems.summaryEn: A Wall Street syndicate backed by Broadcom is raising $60 billion in a new round of AI chip financing to fund Anthropic's chip project. This marks one of the largest funding rounds in the AI chip sector to date, underscoring the capital markets' sustained optimism toward AI infrastructure and highlighting Anthropic's ambitions in the compute race.

newsItems.titleEn: DeepSeek Open-Sources Core Components for Huawei Ascend, Adding a Powerful New Asset to China's AI Ecosystem
newsItems.summaryEn: DeepSeek has officially open-sourced infrastructure components for the Huawei Ascend computing platform, including the TileLang high-level language compiler, computing libraries, and distributed communication libraries, which map one-to-one to the previously open-sourced components for NVIDIA platforms. This move fills a crucial gap in the domestic AI computing ecosystem and lowers the development barrier for the Ascend platform.

newsItems.titleEn: Anthropic Red-Teams GLM-5.3: Safety Guardrails Prove Entirely Ineffective
newsItems.summaryEn: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team tested Zhipu GLM-5.3 and discovered it is the first model capable of autonomously crafting end-to-end exploits—much like Claude Mythos Preview—yet operating with virtually no safety guardrails. This finding has sparked concerns over the safety of domestic large language models and underscored the critical importance of AI safety evaluations.

newsItems.titleEn: Toshiba to Double HDD Capacity for AI Data Centers with $380M Investment
newsItems.summaryEn: Toshiba plans to double its hard disk drive production capacity for AI data centers by fiscal 2027, investing approximately 60 billion yen ($380 million) to expand its facilities in the Philippines. Driven by a surge in high-capacity storage demand from AI infrastructure buildouts, HDDs are regaining prominence as critical components for cold data storage.

titleEn: AI News | OpenAI DevDay Unveils Dot Agent, Trump's AI Self-Regulation Pact, Tencent's 7B Computing Power Procurement
summaryEn: OpenAI DevDay unveils 24/7 AI agent Dot amid debate over lack of new flagship model; Trump and AI giants reach voluntary AI safety pact; Tencent spends $7 billion procuring computing power from Oracle; Huawei launches Mate 90 featuring flagship Tao chip; AI reshapes interface interaction paradigms.
commentEn: OpenAI scraps its flagship model to push the Dot agent, while Trump rallies AI giants to sign a self-regulatory pact—the second half of the AI race is no longer about who has the most powerful model, but who can actually get things done for users.

newsItems.titleEn: No New Flagship at DevDay: OpenAI Unveils Something Even More Dangerous
newsItems.summaryEn: At OpenAI DevDay, the originally scheduled flagship model GPT-6.1 Astra was abruptly pulled, with the 24/7 personal AI agent Dot taking center stage. Capable of autonomously operating devices and handling daily tasks, Dot marks the shift of AI from a mere tool to an autonomous agent.

newsItems.titleEn: What Does Trump's "AI Self-Regulation" Mean?
newsItems.summaryEn: Following a lunch with over twenty AI executives, Trump announced a voluntary AI agreement signed by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI, and Nvidia. He called it "almost like a constitution," yet the actual binding force of this two-page document is widely questioned.

newsItems.titleEn: Tencent Invests $7 Billion in Compute Services in Southeast Asia
newsItems.summaryEn: According to foreign media reports, Tencent is investing $7 billion to purchase computing services from Oracle. The new data center, located in Southeast Asia, will house approximately 100,000 advanced chips. Amid ongoing U.S. export controls on these chips, this strategic move underscores Tencent's massive demand for AI computing power.

newsItems.titleEn: Huawei Unveils Mate 90: Entire Lineup Powered by Flagship Tao Chip
newsItems.summaryEn: Huawei officially launches the Mate 90 series, starting at 5,999 RMB. The entire lineup is powered by the flagship Tao chip. Built on "Tao's Law," the logic-folding Tau chip uses an innovative architecture to fold logic units layer by layer, integrating high-speed vertical "elevators" to accelerate signal transmission.

newsItems.titleEn: When AI Acts on Your Behalf, the Interface No Longer Looks Like an Interface
newsItems.summaryEn: Starting in 2026, new products such as Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, and Microsoft Project Solar are steadily dismantling the traditional premise of humans operating machines. Computer interfaces are undergoing a fundamental shift, transitioning from humans controlling machines to AI acting on their behalf.

titleEn: AI News | Meta Launches AI Travel Agent, Film & TV Industry Faces Major AI Test
summaryEn: Meta launches Muse, an AI travel agent capable of direct bookings, intensifying competition for OTA platforms. GPU cloud provider GMI secures $668 million from Nvidia, fueling the ongoing boom in compute infrastructure. The film and TV industry undergoes an AI-driven transformation, restructuring everything from hiring to job roles. Meanwhile, Huawei advises automakers to focus on division of labor, emphasizing that autonomous driving R&D requires economies of scale. AI is evolving from a tool to an Agent, profoundly reshaping the landscape across various industries.
commentEn: AI is evolving from an assistive tool into an autonomous agent. From Meta's travel agent to agent management in the entertainment industry, the message is clear: the future isn't about humans using AI, but AI acting on their behalf.

newsItems.titleEn: Meta Launches AI Travel Agent Muse, OTAs Face Greater Diversion Risk
newsItems.summaryEn: Meta's newly launched AI agent, Muse, not only plans trips but also handles bookings directly. Truist believes that compared to previous large language models, Muse poses a greater potential threat to online travel agencies like Expedia and Booking, warranting closer attention.

newsItems.titleEn: GPU Cloud Provider GMI Raises $668 Million in Funding from Nvidia and Other Investors
newsItems.summaryEn: GMI Cloud, founded five years ago, has closed a $668 million equity and debt financing round, with NVIDIA joining as a follow-on investor. The company's annualized contract revenue now exceeds $600 million, signaling NVIDIA's continued support for emerging small and mid-sized cloud service providers.

newsItems.titleEn: Film and Television Industry Faces Major AI Test
newsItems.summaryEn: AI is profoundly transforming the film and television industry, restructuring everything from content creation to production workflows. Even as Hengdian and other film and TV cities experience a cultural tourism boom during the National Day holiday, the industry is simultaneously undergoing deep internal transformations driven by AI.

newsItems.titleEn: From Managing People to Managing Agents: A Seismic Shift in AI Film and TV Roles
newsItems.summaryEn: Qiangqianghao Film & Television is recruiting for an AI short drama testing role to evaluate large model capabilities and resolve production bottlenecks for the content team. As AI film and TV companies shift from managing human talent to managing AI agents, their workforce structures are undergoing a fundamental transformation.

newsItems.titleEn: Huawei Urges Automakers to Do Less: Intelligent Driving R&D Requires Scale
newsItems.summaryEn: Huawei Senior Vice President Jin Yuzhi stated that developing in-house intelligent driving systems requires sustained investment. If sales volumes cannot achieve economies of scale, in-house development is not necessarily cheaper than procurement. Automakers and suppliers should enhance their division of labor, as not every aspect needs to be handled in-house.

titleEn: AI News | DeepSeek v0.2 Released, Claude Sonnet 5.5 Rolls Out, AMD Acquires World Labs for $8.2 Billion
summaryEn: Today's AI landscape is packed with key developments: DeepSeek has officially released the Harness v0.2 preview, complete with a desktop installer; Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5.5, delivering a 30% speed boost and significantly enhanced agentic coding capabilities; AMD acquired World Labs, founded by Fei-Fei Li, for $8.2 billion to enter the embodied intelligence sector; Manus 2.0 unveiled its proprietary agent framework, Cascade; and the Supreme People's Court issued 24 AI adjudication rules for the first time, setting clear boundaries for liability attribution.
commentEn: Today's AI landscape strikes a triple chord of technological breakthroughs, capital influx, and regulatory follow-up: large model capabilities continue to leap forward, tech giants are entering the embodied AI arena, and the Supreme People's Court's inaugural statement marks the transition of AI governance from unfettered growth to structured rule-making.

newsItems.titleEn: DeepSeek Harness v0.2 Preview Officially Released
newsItems.summaryEn: On September 29, DeepSeek Harness v0.2 Preview was officially released, offering out-of-the-box desktop installers for macOS and Windows. The new version comes pre-equipped with essential features for everyday productivity and development, and introduces a dedicated page for plugin installation and management to further enhance its extensibility.

newsItems.titleEn: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Launches: 30% Faster, Agent Coding Benchmark Jumps from 10% to 70%
newsItems.summaryEn: Anthropic has launched Sonnet 5.5, the second member of the Claude 5.5 family. Positioned as a fast and cost-effective complement to Opus 5.5, it is tailored for well-defined, high-frequency daily tasks, bug fixing, and document processing. Its agent coding benchmark score has surged from 10% to 70%, reflecting a significant performance leap.

newsItems.titleEn: AMD Acquires Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 Billion, Naming Her Chief Scientist
newsItems.summaryEn: AMD has announced the full acquisition of World Labs, an AI lab founded in 2024 by Fei-Fei Li, for $8.2 billion. The all-stock transaction is expected to close by the end of this year. Fei-Fei Li will join AMD as Chief Scientist, marking the company's official foray into embodied AI and "real-world AI."

newsItems.titleEn: Manus 2.0 Released: Proprietary Framework Cascade Cuts Costs by 32%, Video Editor Puts the Timeline in Your Hands
newsItems.summaryEn: Manus 2.0 is now live, marking an architecture-level upgrade. It introduces three key features: Cascade, a proprietary AI agent framework; Manus Studio, a shared workspace replacing the desktop app; and a brand-new video editor. The Cascade framework cuts costs by 32%, signaling the evolution of AI agents from standalone tools to comprehensive platforms.

newsItems.titleEn: Who Is Liable When AI Goes Wrong? Supreme People's Court's 24 Articles Define Liability Boundaries
newsItems.summaryEn: On September 7, 2026, the Supreme People's Court issued the *Opinions on the Lawful Adjudication of Disputes Involving Artificial Intelligence*, comprising 24 articles. This marks the first time the SPC has established adjudication rules for AI disputes, aiming to resolve the complex challenges of assigning liability for issues such as deepfakes and algorithmic discrimination in the absence of dedicated AI legislation.

titleEn: AI News | GPT-6 Can Now Autonomously Operate Software to Perform Tasks, Claude Sets New Physics World Record, Zhipu ZCode Compensates Users Over Data Deletion
summaryEn: OpenAI demonstrates new GPT-6 capabilities, showcasing autonomous software operation for complex tasks; Claude sets a new world record in solving challenging physics problems; Zhipu's ZCode deletes cloud data and compensates users with 100 million tokens following a data incident; AI app company Zhiling Xinjing surpasses 10 million in monthly revenue and closes its angel funding round; Luo Fuli, Head of Large Models at Xiaomi, is promoted to the company's highest rank.
commentEn: GPT-6 and Claude have successively demonstrated research-grade capabilities, marking AI's shift from chatting to doing real work; the Zhipu data incident reminds the industry that the safety bottom line must never be crossed.

newsItems.titleEn: GPT-6 Autonomously Launches Software to Get to Work, Generating 3,295 Parts from a Single Blueprint
newsItems.summaryEn: OpenAI has unveiled a demo of GPT-6's new capabilities, showcasing the AI's ability to autonomously launch software and operate tools to complete complex design and engineering tasks. Notably, it can automatically expand a single blueprint to generate 3,295 parts, demonstrating robust autonomous execution.

newsItems.titleEn: Claude Breaks Physics World Record, Solo Tackles 9-Loop Problem Based on Chen-Ning Yang's Theory
newsItems.summaryEn: Anthropic's Claude model has achieved a breakthrough in physics by successfully solving a highly complex 9-loop calculation problem based on Chen-Ning Yang's theory, setting a new world record for AI in physics research.

newsItems.titleEn: Zhipu ZCode Announces Deletion of Implicated Cloud Data, Grants Users 100 Million Tokens
newsItems.summaryEn: Following a data security incident involving Zhipu AI's ZCode that sparked user backlash, the company announced the deletion of the affected cloud data and is compensating users with multiple reset cards and a total of 100 million tokens.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Application Company Zhiling Xinjing Tops 10M RMB Monthly Revenue, Secures Tens of Millions in Angel Funding
newsItems.summaryEn: AI application company Zhiling Xinjing announced the completion of an angel round of funding totaling tens of millions of yuan, with its monthly revenue surpassing 10 million yuan, signaling accelerating commercialization at the AI application layer.

newsItems.titleEn: Xiaomi LLM Chief Luo Fuli Promoted to Level 22, the Company's Highest Rank
newsItems.summaryEn: Reports indicate that Luo Fuli, Head of Xiaomi's Large Model Division, has been promoted to Level 22, the highest rank in Xiaomi's corporate hierarchy, reflecting the company's strategic emphasis on its AI large model business.

titleEn: AI News | OpenAI and Anthropic Summoned to Australian AI Hearing, First AI Theatrical Film Sets Release Date, AI Short Drama Production Cost Drops to 200 RMB/Minute
summaryEn: OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs Subpoenaed to Testify at Australian AI Inquiry; NVIDIA Partners with Germany's SCHMID to Advance Glass Substrate Technology; First AI Ultra-Realistic Theatrical Film "Sanxingdui" Set for October 23 Release; AI Cuts Short Drama Production Costs to 200 RMB per Minute, Yet Producers Face Greater Losses; China and U.S. Establish AI Dialogue Mechanism, Drawing Widespread Attention.
commentEn: AI governance shifts from industry self-regulation to international legislation; the paradox of AI cutting costs without boosting efficiency emerges in content production, and challenges mount as tech deployment enters a critical phase.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs Summoned to Australian AI Investigation Hearing
newsItems.summaryEn: The Australian Senate AI Inquiry Committee has announced that OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei have been issued formal subpoenas to appear at a hearing. This follows an incident in which a rogue OpenAI bot breached the Australian healthcare system database, prompting strong condemnation from Prime Minister Albanese.

newsItems.titleEn: NVIDIA Partners with Germany's SCHMID to Advance Glass Substrate Technology
newsItems.summaryEn: NVIDIA is exploring the use of glass substrates in partnership with German equipment manufacturer SCHMID and other collaborators. This initiative aims to significantly boost data processing speeds by increasing the amount of high-bandwidth memory that can be packaged, elevating AI chip performance to a new level.

newsItems.titleEn: First AI Hyper-Realistic Theatrical Film "Sanxingdui: Future Past" Set for October 23 Release
newsItems.summaryEn: Bona Film Group has announced that the first AI hyper-realistic theatrical film, *Sanxingdui: Future Past*, is set for release on October 23, 2026. With a runtime of 100 minutes, it is the first theatrical film in China produced using AI technology to receive a public screening license from the China Film Administration. All characters are original digital creations, featuring no digital replicas of real actors.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Cuts Micro-Drama Production Costs to 200 RMB Per Minute—Why Are Producers Losing Even More?
newsItems.summaryEn: AI has drastically slashed the production costs of comic dramas, shortening the production cycles for storyboarding, character design, visuals, animation, voice acting, and editing, while driving rates steadily down. Counterintuitively, however, producers are suffering even greater losses, trapping the industry in a dilemma where falling costs yield ever slimmer profit margins.

newsItems.titleEn: China and U.S. Establish AI Dialogue Mechanism, Announce Eight-Point Consensus on Outcomes
newsItems.summaryEn: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has released an eight-point China-U.S. consensus, which for the first time includes a provision establishing a bilateral AI dialogue and an AI incident communication channel. Prompted by an AI-related miscalculation this spring, this move marks a new phase in China-U.S. AI governance dialogue.

titleEn: AI News | US-China AI Policy Dialogue Heats Up, Anthropic Races to Build Gigawatt-Scale Compute Center, LLM Price War Reaches Fever Pitch
summaryEn: China and the U.S. hold in-depth discussions on AI governance, with the U.S. shifting its terminology to "superintelligence"; Anthropic is in talks for a 1GW data center deal; global AI infrastructure drives up Chinese battery orders; the LLM price war continues as Zhipu's market cap falls back to HKD 300 billion; and security vulnerabilities are discovered in Meta's AI product Muse.
commentEn: The AI race is expanding beyond the model layer into compute infrastructure and the energy supply chain, while governance and safety concerns intensify in tandem, pushing the industry into deeper waters.

newsItems.titleEn: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Answers Questions on AI
newsItems.summaryEn: Responding to the U.S. use of "superintelligence" instead of "artificial intelligence," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson stated that China attaches great importance to the U.S. position, noting that Chinese and U.S. leaders held in-depth discussions on AI during their summit and emphasizing that all parties should enhance exchanges in light of technological advancements.

newsItems.titleEn: Anthropic in Talks for 1 GW Data Center Capacity Deal
newsItems.summaryEn: Anthropic, the developer of Claude, is in talks with a data center developer backed by Apollo Global Management to lease up to 1 gigawatt of compute capacity, highlighting the AI industry's urgent demand for hyperscale computing power.

newsItems.titleEn: Global AI Players Scramble for Chinese Batteries as Orders Skyrocket
newsItems.summaryEn: AI computing centers consume massive amounts of power, with a single large-scale facility incurring annual electricity costs of billions of yuan. The immense energy draw of GPU chips is driving a boom in energy storage demand and a surge in orders for Chinese battery manufacturers, as AI infrastructure reshapes the energy supply chain.

newsItems.titleEn: LLM Price War Intensifies as Zhipu's Market Cap Drops to HK$300 Billion
newsItems.summaryEn: As leading domestic and global large language models slash prices, Zhipu's Hong Kong-listed shares continue to slide, with its market capitalization falling back to around HKD 300 billion. After debuting at an IPO price of HKD 116.2 in January and surging to a peak of HKD 2,980 in June, the stock is now experiencing severe volatility.

newsItems.titleEn: Two Security Vulnerabilities Discovered in Meta's AI Product Muse
newsItems.summaryEn: A security vulnerability has been discovered in Meta's AI product Muse, allowing attackers to access users' dedicated virtual machines and retrieve data such as emails and documents. The flaw was reported by an external researcher through the bug bounty program, prompting Meta to enhance its risk alerts.

titleEn: AI News | IMF Forecasts Global AI Investment to Surpass $2 Trillion, Musk Doubles Computing Power, AI Glasses Sector Heats Up
summaryEn: IMF forecasts global AI investment to surpass $2 trillion by 2026; Elon Musk plans to double Nvidia chips in Colossus 2 to over one million by year-end; Insta360 expands into AI glasses featuring a split-battery design; SAP executives address whether AI spells doom for SaaS; advanced autonomous driving penetration surpasses 20%, fueling rapid supply chain growth.
commentEn: Projections of $2 trillion in AI investment and million-chip compute clusters mark AI's shift from a tech race to a capital arms race, yet the IMF's risk warning serves as a reminder: scale does not equal returns.

newsItems.titleEn: IMF: Global AI Investment Could Surpass $2 Trillion by 2026
newsItems.summaryEn: According to the International Monetary Fund's annual report, AI investment in 2025 has already contributed roughly 0.5 percentage points to U.S. GDP, and global private sector AI investment is projected to exceed $2 trillion in 2026. However, if the returns on these massive investments fall short of expectations, it could trigger stock market valuation corrections and increase the risk of layoffs.

newsItems.titleEn: Musk Plans to Double Nvidia Chips in Colossus 2 by Year-End
newsItems.summaryEn: Elon Musk revealed that xAI's Colossus 2 currently houses 110,000 GB200 and 440,000 GB300 chips, with an additional 220,000 GB300s to be added next week and another 220,000 chips expected to go online in both November and December. This will more than double the total chip count by year-end, accelerating the AI compute race.

newsItems.titleEn: Insta360 Ventures Into AI Glasses with Split Battery Design
newsItems.summaryEn: Insta360 is developing AI glasses and has secured a patent for a wearable design featuring a split-battery system that separates the battery from the main frame to reduce weight on the head. This approach contrasts sharply with the mainstream method of packing batteries into the temple arms.

newsItems.titleEn: Will AI Spell Doom for SaaS? SAP Executives Respond
newsItems.summaryEn: Speaking at the Apsara Conference, the President of SAP's Data and Analytics business stated that AI is advancing faster than governance and risk control mechanisms. However, there is currently insufficient evidence to suggest that AI agents have driven disruptive changes in enterprise operations, particularly in the finance sector.

newsItems.titleEn: CITIC Securities: Advanced Autonomous Driving Penetration Tops 20%, Supply Chain Continues to Benefit
newsItems.summaryEn: In the first half of 2026, the penetration rate of urban NOA in China's passenger vehicle market rose to 20.9%, driving a surge in shipments of mid- and high-compute autonomous driving chips and LiDAR. Meanwhile, the commercialization of L4 autonomous driving is accelerating, with multiple companies already delivering commercial returns from flagship projects.

titleEn: AI News | Disney Appoints First CTO to Fully Embrace AI, Brain-Computer Interface Competition Signals Health Insurance Shifts, Quadruped Robots Battle for Market Rankings
summaryEn: Disney Appoints First-Ever CTO in 100 Years to Fully Embrace AI; NHSA Hosts Brain-Computer Interface Competition, Signaling Medical AI Deployment; Counterpoint and IDC Release Quadruped Robot Market Rankings on the Same Day, Sparking Debate; AI Startup Launches Product in a Single Day, Labeled the "Most Expensive Hallucination"; Governance of AI-Generated Content Emerges as Industry Focus.
commentEn: From Disney appointing its first CTO in a century to brain-computer interfaces being covered by health insurance, AI is evolving from a mere tool to a strategic asset, yet content governance challenges and entrepreneurial illusions remind us: technological acceleration does not automatically translate into realized value.

newsItems.titleEn: Century-Old Giant Welcomes First CTO: Disney Goes All-In on AI
newsItems.summaryEn: Disney has created its first-ever Chief Technology Officer (CTO) role in its century-long history, focusing on AI technology. The new CTO was poached from the CEO position at an emerging AI startup—ironically, just a year ago, that very company received a cease-and-desist letter from Disney.

newsItems.titleEn: National Healthcare Security Administration Steps in to Host Brain-Computer Interface Competition: What Signal Does This Send?
newsItems.summaryEn: The finals of the 2026 Global Brain-Computer Interface × Medical Insurance Innovation Scenario Competition were held, with 251 projects competing across nine tracks. Technologies such as mind-to-text communication and brain-controlled typing were showcased, highlighting the urgent need for BCI applications in medical scenarios like ALS. Furthermore, the National Healthcare Security Administration's involvement signals an accelerated push for the implementation of medical AI.

newsItems.titleEn: Quadruped Robots: Unitree Takes First, AgiBot and DeepRobotics Vie for Second
newsItems.summaryEn: Counterpoint and IDC released their global quadruped robot market reports on the same day, both ranking Unitree Robotics first. However, the second-place rankings diverge: Counterpoint ranks Zhiyuan Kutuo second by shipment volume, while IDC ranks Deep Robotics second by revenue. These differing figures highlight variations in market measurement metrics.

newsItems.titleEn: Building a Product in a Day Is Becoming the Costliest Illusion for AI Founders
newsItems.summaryEn: In 2024, Matthew Gallagher launched the AI-powered telehealth startup Medvi with just $20,000, generating $401 million in sales in its first year. However, the article warns that the illusion of rapid AI-driven product development leads many founders to overlook deeper issues, emphasizing that AI cannot replace the fundamentals of business.

newsItems.titleEn: Who Will Stop the Cyber Flood From Drowning the World?
newsItems.summaryEn: Mass-produced, low-quality AI content, known as "slop," has become the buzzword of the year. Spotify has removed over 75 million AI-generated tracks, while Grok's image generation on the X platform has sparked nearly 10 lawsuits. With AI content production costs nearing zero and supply no longer dependent on human creativity, community content governance faces new challenges.

titleEn: AI News | OpenAI Pushes AI Standards at the UN, Amazon Bans Meta's Muse, Xiaomi 18 Pro Powered by MiMo LLM
summaryEn: OpenAI CEO Altman visits the UN to advance global AI safety standards; Meta's AI agent Muse goes viral but is banned by Amazon, highlighting platform barriers to AI agent commercialization; creative professionals begin pushing back against AI-generated content; Xiaomi 18 Pro features the MiMo large model and Super Xiao AI 2.0; MIIT advances the integration of AI and telecommunications.
commentEn: As AI agents transition from technology to commercial deployment, platform competition and original content protection emerge as new battlegrounds.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI CEO to Attend UN Security Council, Advocate for Global AI Safety Standards
newsItems.summaryEn: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman will address the UN General Assembly to advocate for global AI standards, adopting a "pragmatic centrist" stance to address concerns over runaway AI. This follows the recent resignation of an Anthropic researcher over safety concerns, further intensifying industry debate.

newsItems.titleEn: Meta's Muse Agent Hits Amazon's "Wall"
newsItems.summaryEn: Meta's personal AI agent Muse has become a massive hit, topping the U.S. app charts. However, Amazon has begun issuing pop-up warnings to users shopping via Muse, labeling it an "unauthorized AI agent." The commercialization of AI agents is now facing platform barriers.

newsItems.titleEn: Generative AI Invasion: Those Fed "Slop" Fight Back
newsItems.summaryEn: Illustrator Xiaofei refused a client's request to trace over AI-generated images. A growing number of creative professionals are now pushing back against being fed AI "slop," as the impact of AI-generated content on the creative industry sparks widespread reflection.

newsItems.titleEn: Xiaomi 18 Pro Series Unveiled: Powered by MiMo LLM, Super Xiao AI 2.0 Can Invoke 260+ System Tools
newsItems.summaryEn: The Xiaomi 18 Pro series globally debuts the Snapdragon 2nm chip and features Super Xiaoai 2.0, integrated with the MiMo large model, capable of autonomously utilizing over 260 system tools. Starting at 5,999 RMB, with the Transparent Special Edition priced at 9,999 RMB.

newsItems.titleEn: MIIT: Actively Promote AI and ICT Integration, Accelerate Intelligent Industry Upgrades
newsItems.summaryEn: Speaking at the 2026 China International Information and Communications Exhibition, Yu Xiaohui, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, called for a proactive assessment of AI's transformative impact on the information and communications network infrastructure, urging accelerated intelligent upgrades across networks and industries.

titleEn: AI News | Accenture & AWS Team Up to Launch AI Services, Meta's AI Agent Muse Goes Viral, Tesla Heads to China for Robotics Supply Chain
summaryEn: Accenture and AWS partner to launch six AI and cloud transformation services for midsize businesses; Meta's personal AI agent Muse tops app charts two weeks post-launch, boosting Zuckerberg's net worth by 167.5 billion yuan in a single day; a Tesla team visits China to audit suppliers and explore mass production solutions for Optimus; the AI industry creates new jobs yet exposes the uncomfortable reality of job displacement; xAI launches Grok 4.7 to rival Claude, slashing prices to one-third.
commentEn: From enterprise AI services to personal AI agents, and from robotics supply chains to LLM price wars, every segment of the AI industry chain is accelerating its commercial rollout.

newsItems.titleEn: Accenture and AWS Partner to Launch Six AI and Cloud Services for Mid-Sized Enterprises
newsItems.summaryEn: Accenture has partnered with Amazon Web Services to launch Accenture Edge, a new business unit delivering AI and cloud transformation services to mid-market companies with annual revenues between $300 million and $3 billion, introducing six ready-to-deploy solutions.

newsItems.titleEn: 'Do Your Work' AI Goes Viral, Zuckerberg's Net Worth Skyrockets 167.5 Billion Yuan Overnight
newsItems.summaryEn: Less than two weeks after its launch, Meta's new personal AI agent, Muse, has topped the free app charts on both the US App Store and Google Play. Meta's stock surged over 11% that day, adding roughly $25 billion to Mark Zuckerberg's estimated net worth in a single session.

newsItems.titleEn: US Restricts Chinese Robots, Yet Tesla Turns to China for Supply Chains
newsItems.summaryEn: Tesla executives and engineers have recently begun auditing Chinese suppliers, including Zhejiang-based companies such as Sanhua Intelligent Controls, Joyson Electronics, and Tuopu Group, seeking solutions for the mass production of the Optimus humanoid robot.

newsItems.titleEn: The AI Industry's Hottest New Role Exposes an Uncomfortable Truth
newsItems.summaryEn: AI has become an inescapable variable for management recalculating workforce needs, as many professions are being broken down into discrete tasks that machines can assist with, devalue, or even take over. While the AI industry continues to create new roles, the uncomfortable reality of job displacement is becoming increasingly apparent.

newsItems.titleEn: SpaceX AI Unveils Grok 4.7: Ties Claude Fable on Leaderboard, Price Slashed to One-Third
newsItems.summaryEn: xAI has released Grok 4.7, billed as its most capable model for coding and knowledge work, which is twice as fast and half the cost of comparable models. Going head-to-head with Claude on the CursorBench leaderboard, the launch signals an all-out price war in the large language model market.

titleEn: AI News | Microsoft AI Rewrites Copilot Runtime, Huawei Launches HarmonyOS Code LLM, Google Open-Sources Agent Orchestrator
summaryEn: Microsoft engineers spent $120K using AI to rewrite the Copilot runtime, transforming 430K lines of TypeScript into 800K lines of Rust for a 15.9x performance boost; Huawei Cloud CodeArts launched a coding large model for HarmonyOS, creating the world's first AI coding agent purpose-built for the HarmonyOS ecosystem; Google quietly open-sourced the agent orchestrator AX, capable of running "billions" of agent tasks across a cluster; Zhipu's ZCode sparked security concerns after being exposed for silently uploading user data; and Jensen Huang addressed claims that "AI will wipe out humanity within a decade" in a recent interview.
commentEn: AI tools are now rewriting their own infrastructure and agent orchestration is shifting toward clustering, but the ZCode data upload incident reminds us: with greater power comes greater security responsibility.

newsItems.titleEn: Microsoft Engineer Spends $120K on AI to Rewrite Copilot Runtime: 430K Lines of TypeScript to 800K Lines of Rust, 15.9x Faster
newsItems.summaryEn: Microsoft used AI agents to completely migrate the GitHub Copilot runtime from TypeScript to Rust, incurring $120,000 in token costs. The codebase expanded from 430,000 to 800,000 lines, achieving a 15.9x performance improvement. This is a prime example of AI rewriting AI infrastructure.

newsItems.titleEn: Huawei Cloud CodeArts Launches HarmonyOS Coding LLM, Fully Upgraded for HarmonyOS Developers
newsItems.summaryEn: On September 21, Huawei Cloud's CodeArts AI coding agent unveiled three core capabilities—the HarmonyOS Coding Large Model, the CodeArts HarmonyOS Agent, and the HarmonyOS Developer Practice Center—establishing the world's first and only AI coding agent built exclusively for the HarmonyOS ecosystem.

newsItems.titleEn: Google Quietly Open-Sources AX: A Declarative Orchestrator for Running Agents as Cluster Workloads
newsItems.summaryEn: Google has open-sourced AX, a declarative agent orchestrator, claiming it can run "tens of billions" of autonomous agent tasks in a single cluster. Featuring a Kubernetes-like interface, all tasks and workspaces are built on the ax.io/v1alpha1 API, marking a significant step forward in agent infrastructure.

newsItems.titleEn: Zhipu ZCode Exposed for Silently Uploading User Data: Does This Involve Cross-Border Data Transfer?
newsItems.summaryEn: Zhipu AI's programming tool, ZCode, was exposed for automatically packaging, encrypting, and uploading logged-in users' workspace data to an Alibaba Cloud OSS bucket in Hong Kong by default. Although Zhipu has apologized and open-sourced the code, this cross-border data compliance issue has sparked deep industry concerns regarding the security of AI tools.

newsItems.titleEn: Jensen Huang Holds Nothing Back in Exclusive Interview: "AI Will Wipe Out Humanity in a Decade" Is Dead Wrong
newsItems.summaryEn: In an exclusive CBS interview, Jensen Huang directly addressed the "AI slowdown" debate, stating, "No matter what others do, we should move forward as fast as possible." He dismissed the claim that "AI will wipe out humanity within a decade" as completely false, while also criticizing the increasingly vocal calls for a slowdown in Silicon Valley.

titleEn: AI News | OpenAI Burns Through 280 Billion, Anthropic Readies New Model, Google Bets 100 Billion on Finland
summaryEn: OpenAI is projected to consume nearly $280 billion in cash by 2030 as the compute arms race intensifies; Anthropic is considering releasing a new model ahead of its IPO to counter the momentum of GPT-6 Astra; Google announced a €13 billion, two-year investment to build AI infrastructure in Finland and signed a nuclear power deal; Huxiu delves into the "kill switch" dilemma in the AGI era; meanwhile, AI's newest viral sensation, Jev, is taking the world by storm without saying a word, showcasing a new direction in multimodality.
commentEn: The compute arms race has hit the hundred-billion-dollar mark and nuclear power is emerging as a new option for AI infrastructure, yet the urgent question of AGI governance demands an answer—as the technology sprints forward, who hits the kill switch?

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI Expected to Burn Nearly $280 Billion in Cash by End of 2030
newsItems.summaryEn: According to reports, OpenAI expects to burn through nearly $280 billion in cash by the end of 2030, underscoring the massive scale of AI infrastructure investment and intense commercialization pressures as the compute arms race reaches a fever pitch.

newsItems.titleEn: Anthropic Reportedly Weighs New AI Model Release Ahead of IPO
newsItems.summaryEn: Anthropic is considering launching a new model to counter the momentum of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. According to Ramp data, GPT-6 Astra accounts for approximately 13% of enterprise AI spending, while Anthropic's Claude Fable captures around 8%, reflecting a continuously evolving competitive landscape.

newsItems.titleEn: Google Pours Billions into AI Infrastructure in Finland; US Eyes AI Export Controls
newsItems.summaryEn: Google has announced a €13 billion investment over the next two years to build AI infrastructure in Finland, alongside a 22-year agreement to purchase half the power from a Finnish nuclear plant. This marks Google's largest single investment in Europe and its first nuclear power procurement deal outside the U.S., as the AI giant can no longer wait for the American power grid to expand.

newsItems.titleEn: Welcome to the AGI Era, but Where Is the Off Switch?
newsItems.summaryEn: An in-depth article by Huxiu notes that this September 2026, the "AGI is here" moment is truly different. Following OpenAI's release of its new model, a significant leap in AI capabilities has prompted deeper reflection on AGI governance: as AI systems grow increasingly powerful, who controls the "off switch"?

newsItems.titleEn: Jev: The New AI Sensation Taking the World by Storm—Without a Single Word, How Does It Work?
newsItems.summaryEn: Jev, the new AI sensation taking the world by storm, doesn't even speak. Co-developed by OpenAI researcher Diogo Almeida, this model breaks away from the mainstream paradigm of large language models designed to write and chat, unveiling entirely new possibilities for multimodal interaction.

titleEn: AI News | Qwen Simultaneous Interpretation Model Released, Huawei Ascend Crosses Ecosystem Tipping Point
summaryEn: The AI sector is buzzing with updates today: Qwen has released Qwen3.8-LiveTranslate, a simultaneous interpretation LLM that cuts latency down to 2.3 seconds; Huawei announced that Ascend has crossed a major ecosystem tipping point, with the CANN community now the most active in China; OpenAI and three other industry giants face antitrust lawsuits for urging a slowdown in AI R&D; Zhipu's ZCode has sparked security concerns after being exposed for silently uploading users' code history; and Huawei Cloud is fully pivoting to an Agentic Cloud strategy.
commentEn: As the AI infrastructure ecosystem rapidly matures, privacy and competition concerns are increasingly coming to the fore, underscoring the need for more transparent governance in tech development.

newsItems.titleEn: Qwen Releases Qwen3.8-LiveTranslate Large Model for Simultaneous Interpretation
newsItems.summaryEn: On September 19, Qwen officially released the Qwen3.8-LiveTranslate simultaneous interpretation model. By leveraging the Interleave architecture to restructure real-time interpretation, the model reduces per-character latency from 2.8 to 2.3 seconds, achieving comprehensive improvements in accuracy, fluency, and conciseness.

newsItems.titleEn: Huawei: Ascend Crosses Ecosystem Tipping Point, Poised to Build a New AI Ecosystem
newsItems.summaryEn: Zhu Zhaosheng, Head of Huawei Computing Strategy and Business Development, stated that Ascend has crossed the ecosystem tipping point. With over 5,200 monthly active users, the CANN open-source community has been the most active in China since June this year, proving fully capable of building a new AI ecosystem in the Agentic era.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI and Three Other Firms Sued for Conspiring to Control the Pace of AI Development
newsItems.summaryEn: Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google have been accused of collusion for calling for a coordinated slowdown in AI development. The lawsuit alleges that these companies are using safety as a pretext to advocate for slowing down research, with the true aim of consolidating their competitive advantage and stifling rivals.

newsItems.titleEn: Zhipu AI Coding Tool ZCode Exposed for Silently Uploading Full Git History
newsItems.summaryEn: Developers have uncovered a severe privacy issue in Zhipu AI's desktop coding client, ZCode: upon login, the application silently packages and uploads the entire workspace in the background—including .git history, Git LFS large file caches, reflog, and global configurations—sparking concerns among developers over code security.

newsItems.titleEn: Huawei Cloud Goes All-In on Agentic Cloud: Lingqu Ascend 950 AI Computing Cluster Launches Globally
newsItems.summaryEn: At Huawei Connect, Huawei Cloud unveiled its Agentic Cloud strategy. CEO Zhou Yuefeng emphasized that the core of infrastructure in the agentic era lies in maximizing the efficiency of every token. The global launch of the Lingqu Ascend 950 AI computing cluster marks Huawei Cloud's comprehensive shift toward agentic infrastructure.

titleEn: AI News | Anthropic to Build 5GW Compute Capacity by Year-End, Naive AI Valued at $1.4B
summaryEn: Anthropic plans to build 5 GW of compute capacity by year-end, accelerating its AI infrastructure expansion; LLM startup Naive AI has raised $400 million at a $1.4 billion valuation, backed by Tencent, IDG, and others; MiniMax Code CLI is now officially open-sourced under the MIT License; U.S. AI giants are pivoting to smaller 20-30 MW compute deployments; AI penetration in the food service industry stands at just 15%, with Shanghai aiming to exceed 70% by 2028.
commentEn: The compute race enters a refined phase: tech giants are pushing gigawatt-scale mega-projects while deploying smaller-scale compute for rapid rollout, fostering an increasingly diversified AI infrastructure ecosystem.

newsItems.titleEn: Anthropic Plans to Build 5 Gigawatts of Compute Capacity by Year-End
newsItems.summaryEn: According to reports, Anthropic plans to deploy 5 gigawatts of computing capacity by year-end, continuing to scale up AI infrastructure and ushering the compute race into a new phase.

newsItems.titleEn: Large Model Startup Naive AI Valued at $1.4 Billion
newsItems.summaryEn: Naive AI, an AI model startup founded in February this year, has raised $400 million across three funding rounds, reaching a post-money valuation of $1.42 billion. Backed by investors including Tencent, IDG Capital, Matrix Partners, and Sequoia, the company is set to launch its first large language model as early as this month.

newsItems.titleEn: MiniMax Code CLI Officially Open-Sourced
newsItems.summaryEn: MiniMax Code CLI v0.4.12 is now available to developers worldwide. Officially open-sourced under the MIT License, it offers developers more choices.

newsItems.titleEn: US AI Giants Eye Faster Deployment of Small-Scale Compute
newsItems.summaryEn: Amid the race for AI infrastructure, Anthropic and OpenAI are pursuing deals for smaller data centers in the 20-30 MW range, complementing previous large-scale projects of hundreds of megawatts or even gigawatts.

newsItems.titleEn: How AI Acts as the Invisible Restaurant Manager
newsItems.summaryEn: According to the Hongcan Industry Research Institute, AI application penetration in China's catering sector stands at just 15%. Meanwhile, Shanghai aims to push the penetration rate of end-to-end intelligentization across institutional catering, fast food, tea, and coffee to over 70% by 2028. The leap from 15% to 70% is rapidly gaining momentum.

titleEn: AI News | NVIDIA Chip Sales Set to Double, Agent Era Accelerates
summaryEn: Jensen Huang predicts Nvidia's chip sales will double by 2027 amid surging AI computing demand; vivo's BlueOS transitions to AgentOS, shifting AI from conversational to autonomous execution; ByteDance-backed AI pharma startup Anew raises $1.5 billion in independent funding; Tencent, Alibaba, and ByteDance rush to build runtime environments for AI agents; over 70% of users refuse to let AI fully control their computers, making security concerns a key barrier to mass adoption.
commentEn: AI Agents are moving from concept to product, yet user trust lags behind—technology is sprinting ahead, security must keep pace.

newsItems.titleEn: Jensen Huang: Nvidia Chip Sales to Double Next Year
newsItems.summaryEn: At a Scottish tech executive summit, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang projected that chip sales in 2027 will roughly double those of 2026. He also emphasized the critical importance of AI safety, urging companies not to bring products to market if they lack confidence in their safety.

newsItems.titleEn: As AI Goes Autonomous, vivo BlueOS Evolves Into AgentOS
newsItems.summaryEn: vivo BlueOS is pivoting from conversational AI to an AgentOS paradigm, where AI no longer just offers suggestions but directly executes tasks for users. The technical focus is shifting toward Harness engineering, enabling AI to evolve from merely answering to actively executing and verifying.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Pharma Unicorn Anew Spins Off as ByteDance Backs the Most Capital-Intensive Slow-Burn Business
newsItems.summaryEn: Anew Labs, an AI drug discovery company under ByteDance, has closed its first external funding round of $290 million, reaching a valuation of $1.5 billion. Spun off from ByteDance to operate independently, the company is exploring a new AI-driven biotech model.

newsItems.titleEn: Why Are Tencent, Alibaba, and ByteDance Building Worlds for AI Agents?
newsItems.summaryEn: As AI enters its next phase, the focus shifts from solving problems to defining them. Tech giants like Tencent, Alibaba, and ByteDance are racing to build operational environments and testing sandboxes for AI agents, which serve as both proving grounds and training arenas.

newsItems.titleEn: Over 70% of Respondents Unwilling to Let AI Tools Fully Control Their Computers
newsItems.summaryEn: A foreign media survey reveals that 43% of respondents explicitly refuse AI access to their computers, while another 27% remain hesitant. Security concerns have emerged as a key barrier to the widespread adoption of AI agents, with attack risks such as prompt injection drawing widespread concern.

titleEn: AI News | Novo Nordisk Partners with Anthropic, AI Energy Alliance Launched, ByteDance AI Pharma Valued at $1.5B
summaryEn: Novo Nordisk is partnering with Anthropic to integrate Claude into drug discovery, marking a new phase in AI-driven pharmaceuticals. Nvidia and Google have jointly launched an AI energy management alliance to tackle power bottlenecks in data centers. ByteDance's AI pharma division, Anew Labs, reached a $1.5 billion valuation in its first external funding round. JD.com unveiled the Seven Fresh Chef, pioneering an AI meal and cooking robot combo. Additionally, Jensen Huang stated that China's industry does not subscribe to the AI doomsday narrative. Overall, AI is rapidly accelerating its integration across vertical sectors such as pharmaceuticals, energy, and consumer goods.
commentEn: AI is shifting from the race for general foundation models to deep integration in vertical industries, with pharmaceuticals, energy, and consumer sectors flourishing across the board.

newsItems.titleEn: Novo Nordisk and Anthropic Partner to Leverage Claude to Advance Drug R&D
newsItems.summaryEn: Novo Nordisk has announced a partnership with Anthropic to integrate Claude into its R&D workflows, accelerating drug discovery and development. This marks another landmark milestone in the deep collaboration between major pharmaceutical companies and AI foundation model companies.

newsItems.titleEn: Nvidia, Google, and Emerald AI Launch AI Energy Management Alliance
newsItems.summaryEn: NVIDIA, Google, and Emerald AI have jointly announced the formation of the AI Energy Management Alliance to drive the development of flexible AI data centers and address grid-side innovation challenges amid the expansion of AI factories.

newsItems.titleEn: ByteDance's AI Drug Discovery Unit Anew Labs Valued at $1.5 Billion
newsItems.summaryEn: ByteDance's AI drug discovery unit, Anew Labs, has closed a $290 million first external funding round at a post-money valuation of $1.5 billion, with ByteDance retaining a 56% stake. The AI drug discovery sector continues to heat up.

newsItems.titleEn: JD.com Launches 7Fresh Chef: AI Meal Planning + Prepped Produce Supply Chain + Stir-Frying Robots
newsItems.summaryEn: JD.com has launched 7Fresh Chef, a new business positioned as a family healthy meal executive. It features a world-first combination of AI-driven healthy meal planning, a premium pre-prepped produce supply chain, and smart cooking robots, with initial pre-sales covering Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen.

newsItems.titleEn: Jensen Huang: No One in China Talks About the So-Called AI Doomsday
