newsItems.summaryEn: DeepSeek announced adjustments to its API pricing rules effective August 23, eliminating peak and off-peak distinctions on weekends to apply a uniform off-peak rate all day Saturday and Sunday. This move reduces developers' weekend API usage costs, reflecting the broader industry trend of continuously declining AI inference costs.

newsItems.titleEn: Zhongcheng Hualong Launches HL200 Inference Chip: 5.12 TFLOPS/W Energy Efficiency, Cluster Scales Up to 10,000 Cards
newsItems.summaryEn: Zhongcheng Hualong has unveiled the new HL200 inference chip and a supernode AI computing cluster solution. Each card delivers 4 PFLOPS of FP4 performance and 2 PFLOPS of FP8 performance, achieving an energy efficiency of 5.12 TFLOPS/W. Scalable up to 10,000 cards, the cluster is designed for large-scale inference deployments, marking the latest addition to the domestic AI chip lineup.

newsItems.titleEn: Tesla Sets September 3 for Cybercab Autonomous EV Reveal
newsItems.summaryEn: Tesla has announced it will host the Cybercab launch event on September 3, 2026, in Austin, Texas. The fully AI-driven vehicle features no steering wheel, pedals, or rearview mirrors, and officially entered production in North America this April. The commercialization of autonomous driving continues to accelerate.

newsItems.titleEn: Meituan Executives Reflect on 'Company-Wide Shrimp Farming': 80,000 Employees Consume Tens of Millions in Daily Compute Without Boosting Productivity
newsItems.summaryEn: Wang Puzhong, CEO of Meituan's Core Local Business, publicly reviewed the internal AI campaign dubbed "Raising Shrimp for All." From February to March this year, approximately 80,000 employees were granted unrestricted access to AI agents with no token limits. However, daily compute consumption in the tens of millions failed to yield the expected productivity gains. This case highlights the real-world challenges of enterprise AI adoption.

titleEn: AI News | Stripe Acquires OpenRouter in Sky-High Deal, DeepSeek Bolsters Vision Capabilities, $3 Trillion AI Infrastructure Debt Raises Alarms
summaryEn: Stripe plans to acquire model routing platform OpenRouter for over $7 billion, marking the payment giant's official entry into the AI infrastructure layer; DeepSeek releases an experimental vision model, V4-Flash, with multimodal capabilities nearing Opus-level performance; The Wall Street Journal warns that the AI infrastructure boom is generating $3 trillion in hidden debt, sparking subprime crisis fears; OSChina reports that the OpenConnector gateway enables AI agents to securely access thousands of SaaS services; and Bloomberg data reveals that the AI gap between China and the U.S. is rapidly narrowing.
commentEn: The AI industry is shifting from a "model race" to an "infrastructure consolidation" phase—evidenced by Stripe's massive acquisition of a routing platform and the surfacing of $3 trillion in debt, all pointing to one conclusion: the next AI battleground lies not in the models themselves, but in who can most efficiently and securely turn them into tangible productivity.

newsItems.titleEn: Why Stripe Is Eyeing Model Routing: AI Enters the Era of Intelligent Procurement
newsItems.summaryEn: Stripe is reportedly planning to acquire OpenRouter for over $7 billion—a model routing platform that neither trains models nor requires GPUs. Developers can access models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers through a single API integration. This move by the payments giant marks a shift in the AI industry from a "model race" to "intelligent procurement," positioning model routing as a new infrastructure layer.

newsItems.titleEn: DeepSeek V4-Flash Gains Vision Capabilities, Multimodal Agent Approaches Opus 4.8
newsItems.summaryEn: DeepSeek has released the experimental vision version of V4-Flash (deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp), now available via API. Building on its already outstanding performance in text-only tasks, the newly added vision capabilities bring its multimodal agent performance close to that of Claude Opus 4.8, marking further progress in the multimodal race among China's large language models.

newsItems.titleEn: $3 Trillion in Hidden Debt Surfaces: Will the AI Infrastructure Boom Trigger the Next Subprime Crisis?
newsItems.summaryEn: An analysis of regulatory filings by The Wall Street Journal across nine major tech companies, including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta, reveals that the AI infrastructure investment boom is generating approximately $3 trillion in hidden debt. AI-related risks are now extending beyond tech stock valuations into infrastructure debt, leading some analysts to draw parallels with the leverage build-up preceding the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis.

newsItems.titleEn: Open-Source Connector Gateway OpenConnector: Enabling AI Agents to Securely Access 1,000+ SaaS Services
newsItems.summaryEn: Oomol Lab has open-sourced OpenConnector, a connector gateway for AI agents that addresses authentication, access control, API adaptation, and runtime auditing challenges when integrating with external SaaS services. By connecting existing application accounts to a unified runtime and exposing standardized capabilities to agents, it significantly lowers the barrier to deploying enterprise-grade AI agents.

newsItems.titleEn: The US-China AI Gap Is Disappearing: Not a Prediction, It's Happening Now
newsItems.summaryEn: On August 20, Bloomberg Businessweek published a special report using over a dozen charts to compare model capabilities, costs, downloads, and regional market shares, revealing that the U.S. lead over China in the AI race is rapidly shrinking. Backed by extensive data covering multiple key metrics, the report has sparked widespread industry discussion.

titleEn: AI News | Alibaba's AI Revenue Surges, Domestic Chip Breakthroughs Accelerate
summaryEn: Alibaba's AI annualized revenue surpasses 49.5 billion RMB, with the CEO projecting it will near $10 billion next quarter; Meta becomes Microsoft's largest AI client, with annual spending reaching hundreds of millions of dollars; T-Head's second-generation AI chip will be taped out in the second half of the year, serving as a robust alternative for large-scale model training; Vercel launches a lightweight browser-based agent tool; WRC 2026 focuses on haptic technology to enhance world models' understanding of physics.
commentEn: AI commercialization is entering a breakout phase: revenue data from tech giants validates returns on tech investments, while breakthroughs in domestic chips and tool innovations signal a maturing ecosystem.

newsItems.titleEn: Alibaba's AI Annualized Revenue Tops 49.5 Billion Yuan
newsItems.summaryEn: Alibaba's Q1 FY2027 earnings report reveals that Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) from AI-related products has surpassed RMB 49.5 billion ($7.3 billion), accounting for 35% of Alibaba Cloud's external commercial revenue. CEO Wu Yongming projects that AI-related product ARR will approach $10 billion next quarter, highlighting the high certainty of returns on AI computing investments and noting that capital expenditures will be recouped within three years.

newsItems.titleEn: Meta Becomes One of Microsoft's Largest AI Customers
newsItems.summaryEn: According to Bloomberg, Meta is procuring AI services via Microsoft Azure, with annual spending reaching hundreds of millions of dollars, making it one of Microsoft's largest AI customers. Meta consumes trillions of tokens per week through Azure, underscoring the massive demand for AI computing power among Big Tech companies.

newsItems.titleEn: T-Head's Second-Generation AI Chip Expected to Tape Out in the Second Half of the Year
newsItems.summaryEn: Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu announced that T-Head's second-generation domestically developed AI chips are expected to begin tape-out and production in the second half of this year. Boasting exceptional computing power and interconnect bandwidth, they are fully capable of supporting large-scale model training. Additionally, supernode instances powered by the new-generation T-Head Zhenwu M890 chip are now available on Alibaba Cloud for large-scale sales.

newsItems.titleEn: Vercel Releases fx: A Lightweight Agent Built in Zig
newsItems.summaryEn: Vercel has open-sourced a new coding agent, fx. Written in Zig, the 6.39MB binary runs in the browser and features a 10-microsecond cold start. Its output style mimics a Unix shell rather than a heavy TUI, offering developers a lightweight AI coding assistant.

newsItems.titleEn: WRC 2026: Tactile Sensing Makes World Models More Physics-Aware
newsItems.summaryEn: The 2026 World Robot Conference highlights new shifts in the tactile sensing sector, where competition is expanding from sensor hardware to the entire pipeline of data collection, model training, and capability evaluation. Tactile sensing bridges the gap for purely vision-based models that can see but not feel, enabling world models to achieve a deeper understanding of the physical world.

titleEn: AI News | Google Taps Marvell for Custom AI Chips, JD.com Bets Billions on Robotics, Kunlun Tech AI Revenue Surges, Kling AI Secures Independent Funding, Nebius Issues $4.5B Compute Bonds
summaryEn: Marvell and Google strike deal for custom AI chips, including TPU inference accelerators; JD.com unveils robotics strategy, investing 10 billion yuan to build a global after-sales network; Kunlun Tech posts 43% H1 revenue growth, with Tiangong AI as its core growth engine; Kuaishou's Kling AI closes independent funding round to optimize compute allocation; AI compute leasing firm Nebius plans to issue $4.5 billion in convertible bonds to expand capacity.
commentEn: From custom chip development to robot deployment, and from large model commercialization to computing power capitalization, all segments of the AI industry chain are accelerating in tandem.

newsItems.titleEn: Marvell and Google Reach Commercial Agreement on Custom AI Chips, Covering TPU Inference Accelerators
newsItems.summaryEn: Marvell Technology has announced a commercial agreement with Google to develop custom semiconductor products, covering TPU ecosystem initiatives including AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, and network interface controllers. Marvell has also issued warrants to Google, allowing the purchase of up to 58.97 million shares at an exercise price of $206.58.

newsItems.titleEn: JD.com Unveils Robotics Strategy: 10 Billion Yuan Investment to Build 80 RoboBase Hubs
newsItems.summaryEn: At the 2026 World Robot Conference, JD.com unveiled its strategic robotics plan. By 2028, the company will invest 10 billion yuan to help 100 brands surpass 1 billion yuan in sales. Over the next five years, it will build after-sales service capabilities covering over 100 countries globally and establish 80 RoboBase facilities. Furthermore, JoyInside is expected to connect more than 10 million end devices by the end of the year.

newsItems.titleEn: Kunlun Tech H1 Revenue Surges 43% to 5.359 Billion RMB; Tiangong AI Emerges as Core Growth Engine
newsItems.summaryEn: Kunlun Tech has released its 2026 semi-annual report, posting revenue of RMB 5.359 billion, up 43.55% year-on-year, with overseas revenue reaching RMB 5.203 billion, a 51% increase. Revenue from the Tiangong AI business has grown quarter-on-quarter, emerging as a key growth driver. The company has upgraded its "4+3" strategy, leveraging four SOTA models—video, music, gaming, and foundation—to power three core platforms: AI short dramas, AI music, and AI gaming.

newsItems.titleEn: Kuaishou's Kling AI Secures Independent Funding, to Optimize Compute Allocation via Leasing
newsItems.summaryEn: At the Q2 earnings call, Kuaishou CFO Jin Bing announced that Kling AI has secured independent funding. The company will adopt a more flexible approach to compute spending, utilizing methods such as leasing to meet growing computing needs and optimize capital allocation. Kuaishou reported positive free cash flow in Q2 and aims to sustain this momentum into the second half of the year.

newsItems.titleEn: AI Compute Leasing Provider Nebius to Issue $4.5 Billion in Convertible Senior Notes
newsItems.summaryEn: AI compute leasing provider Nebius plans to issue $4.5 billion in convertible senior notes to expand its AI compute infrastructure. This move reflects the sustained surge in global demand for AI compute, as specialized compute service providers accelerate capital operations to capture market share.

titleEn: AI News | Baidu AI Revenue Tops 50%, Major Google AI Restructuring, GitHub Down for 7 Hours, Unitree Technology Goes Public Today, AI Optical Materials Surge
summaryEn: Baidu's AI revenue share reached 50% in Q2 and GPU cloud revenue surged 283%, with Ernie returning to the top tier; Google overhauls its AI division, with Brin personally overseeing DeepMind; GitHub suffered an outage lasting over 7 hours on Monday as AI coding demand overwhelmed its infrastructure; Unitree Robotics debuted on the STAR Market today, becoming the first humanoid robot stock on the A-share market; soaring AI compute demand pushes indium phosphide substrate prices up by over 10% again in Q4, with Jensen Huang personally securing supplies.
commentEn: Baidu's AI revenue surpassing 50% signals that domestic tech giants have entered the deep waters of transformation, while Google's AI restructuring underscores the organizational toll even industry leaders pay for their AI strategies; meanwhile, the GitHub outage and surging optical material prices expose the vulnerability of AI infrastructure on both the hardware and software fronts.

newsItems.titleEn: Baidu Q2: AI Revenue Hits 50%, GPU Cloud Surges 283%, ERNIE Set to Return to AI's Top Tier
newsItems.summaryEn: Baidu released its Q2 2026 earnings, reporting total revenue of 31.3 billion yuan. AI business revenue accounted for over half of the total for two consecutive quarters. Within its AI cloud infrastructure, GPU cloud revenue surged 283% year-on-year, marking four consecutive quarters of triple-digit growth. Robin Li stated that the ERNIE large model will return to the top tier of AI, and the company will complete its primary listing in Hong Kong by year-end.

newsItems.titleEn: Inside Google's AI Restructuring: Founder Brin Takes Direct Command Amid DeepMind Power Shuffle
newsItems.summaryEn: Reuters exclusively reports that in April, Google co-founder Sergey Brin called an impromptu meeting to personally intervene in model training, sidelining the godfather of deep learning and prompting two founding technical leads to depart and launch their own startups. This follows months of turmoil and a sweeping organizational restructuring within Google's AI division.

newsItems.titleEn: GitHub Down for Over 7 Hours: AI Coding Frenzy Overwhelms Infrastructure
newsItems.summaryEn: GitHub experienced a major outage on the evening of August 17, lasting over seven hours until services were restored at 5:15 a.m. on August 18. All core features, including the website, API, PRs, and Actions, were affected. The developer community is once again exploring alternative solutions, with self-hosted GitLab and Forgejo frequently mentioned.

newsItems.titleEn: Unitree Robotics Debuts on STAR Market as A-Shares' First Humanoid Robot Stock
newsItems.summaryEn: On August 19, Unitree Robotics officially listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market, becoming the first humanoid robot concept stock in the A-share market. Founder Wang Xingxing shared that he has been passionate about robotics since childhood and had already foreseen the direction and trends of technological development as early as 2016.

newsItems.titleEn: Jensen Huang Personally Scrambles for Supplies as AI Optical Interconnect Material Indium Phosphide Sees Record Price Surge
newsItems.summaryEn: Surging demand for high-speed optical interconnects in AI data centers may push indium phosphide substrate and epitaxial wafer prices up by over 10% in Q4, marking the largest single increase in recent years. Moving beyond shortages of chips, power, and memory, AI computing bottlenecks are now cascading further upstream to optical interconnect materials.

titleEn: AI News | OpenAI Aggressively Expands Infrastructure, Cursor Challenges GitHub, Unitree Robotics Set for IPO
summaryEn: OpenAI and NVIDIA are partnering to build a hyperscale AI data center in Ohio, with investments reaching the hundred-billion-dollar scale; capitalizing on a GitHub outage, Cursor launches Origin, its built-in code hosting platform; Unitree Robotics lists on the STAR Market on August 19, becoming the first humanoid robot stock on China's A-share market; SoftBank invests $200 million in a construction robotics firm; and OpenAI's President addresses the recent wave of executive departures, stating it is nothing out of the ordinary.
commentEn: The AI infrastructure arms race accelerates as OpenAI's hundred-billion-dollar data center push underscores that compute remains the core battlefield; meanwhile, capitalizing on the momentum, Cursor is entering the code hosting space, reshaping the developer tools landscape.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI and Nvidia Expand Partnership, Computing Scale Could Reach $600 Billion by 2030
newsItems.summaryEn: OpenAI will build a world-class AI factory at the PORTS-Pike project in Ohio, leveraging NVIDIA's full-stack DSX AI factory platform with an initial deployment providing 4.25 gigawatts of AI factory capacity. NVIDIA is investing $1.5 billion in SB Energy to support the project.

newsItems.titleEn: Amid GitHub Outage, Cursor Launches Built-In Code Hosting Platform Origin
newsItems.summaryEn: Amid a severe service outage at GitHub, AI coding tool Cursor has announced the launch of Origin—a code hosting platform integrated directly into the editor—in a direct challenge to GitHub.

newsItems.titleEn: A-Shares Welcome First Humanoid Robot Stock: Unitree Robotics to List on STAR Market Aug. 19
newsItems.summaryEn: Unitree Robotics has announced it will list on the STAR Market of the Shanghai Stock Exchange on August 19, 2026, becoming the first humanoid robot concept stock in the A-share market. The company's IPO subscription previously opened on August 10.

newsItems.titleEn: SoftBank Invests $200 Million in Construction Robotics Firm Gravis Robotics
newsItems.summaryEn: Gravis Robotics has closed a $200 million Series A round backed by SoftBank, marking the largest Series A investment in the construction robotics sector. The funds will be used to advance the automation of heavy construction machinery and expand deployments at construction sites worldwide.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI President Responds to Executive Exodus: Not Entirely Unusual
newsItems.summaryEn: OpenAI President Greg Brockman has downplayed market concerns over a string of executive departures, stating that such personnel changes are not unusual and that every exit draws attention simply because OpenAI is under an intense spotlight.

titleEn: AI News | DeepSeek V4 Price Adjustments Signal Pricing Maturity + Anthropic CEO Pens Long Post Addressing Concerns + OpenAI Disbands Risk Mitigation Team + Participation Doubles at Humanoid Robot Games + Baidu Kuku AI Hits 25M MAU
summaryEn: Top 5 AI Industry Highlights Today: The entire DeepSeek V4 series sees early-morning price adjustments as China's AI pricing strategy matures, turning "intelligence" into a commodity; ahead of a 2 trillion valuation IPO, Anthropic's CEO publishes a rare long post addressing doubts, predicting AI will cure most diseases within 5 to 10 years; as OpenAI gears up for its IPO, it disbands its risk prevention team amid ongoing safety architecture adjustments; the 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games is set to open with participation doubling from the inaugural event; and Baidu officially names its AI office agent "Kuku AI," which now boasts over 25 million monthly active users.
commentEn: DeepSeek adjusts prices, Anthropic eyes a $2 trillion valuation, and OpenAI dismantles its safety team—as the AI industry simultaneously accelerates commercialization and restructures its governance, balancing the scales between "affordable and effective" and "safe and controllable" will dictate the industry's trajectory in the next phase.

newsItems.titleEn: DeepSeek V4 Full Lineup Adjusts Prices Overnight as China's AI Pricing Matures
newsItems.summaryEn: Effective midnight on August 17, the new peak and off-peak pricing for the full DeepSeek V4 lineup officially took effect. Over the past year, Chinese models have consistently driven down the cost of frontier intelligence, with their token share on OpenRouter now surpassing that of U.S. models. Analysts note that DeepSeek's price hike signals China is transforming "intelligence" into an industrial commodity, marking the maturation of AI pricing strategies.

newsItems.titleEn: Anthropic CEO Publishes Rare Long-Form Essay to Address Criticism, Predicts AI Will Cure Most Diseases in 5-10 Years
newsItems.summaryEn: With Anthropic's IPO valuation surging to $2 trillion, CEO Dario Amodei has published a rare, lengthy essay directly addressing skepticism from Silicon Valley. He predicts that AI will cure most diseases within the next five to ten years, while also addressing controversies surrounding Anthropic's safety philosophy. This serves as a key signal ahead of the company's largest-ever IPO.

newsItems.titleEn: OpenAI Disbands Risk Preparedness Team Amid IPO Preparations
newsItems.summaryEn: According to the Financial Times, OpenAI disbanded its risk preparedness team at the end of last month. The team's core mission was to assess models for significant risks and develop mitigation strategies. These responsibilities have since been divided across specialized domains such as biosecurity and cybersecurity and absorbed into existing business teams. This follows OpenAI's earlier dissolution of the AGI Readiness Team and the Superalignment Team.

newsItems.titleEn: 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games Set to Open, Participation Doubles
newsItems.summaryEn: The 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games will open on August 22 at the National Speed Skating Oval in Beijing, featuring 51 events and 1,301 matches. A total of 666 teams and 2,056 robots from 16 countries across six continents will compete, marking a 138% increase in teams and a fourfold increase in robots compared to the inaugural edition. All teams have now entered the final sprint phase of training.

newsItems.titleEn: Baidu Unveils Chinese Name "KuKu AI" for GenFlow AI Office Agent; MAU Tops 25 Million
newsItems.summaryEn: At Baidu AI Day, GenFlow, the general-purpose AI agent under Baidu Wenku and Netdisk, officially unveiled its Chinese name, "Kuku AI," alongside the announcement that its AI office products have surpassed 25 million monthly active users. Analysts note that Kuku AI essentially repackages Baidu's decade-long reserves of content and data storage assets within an AI wrapper, signaling intensifying competition in the AI office productivity sector.

titleEn: AI News | SpaceX Acquires Cursor for $60B + Anthropic Eyes History's Largest IPO at $2T Valuation + Unitree IPO Allotment Rate at 0.018% + Qwen Office Launches GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro + Jensen Huang Unveils AI Compute Residual Value Guarantee
summaryEn: Today's Top 5 AI Industry Highlights: SpaceX has officially completed its acquisition of Cursor's parent company, Anysphere, for $60 billion, securing Elon Musk's most strategic asset in the AI coding race; Anthropic could go public as early as October at a $2 trillion investor valuation, surpassing SpaceX to become the largest IPO in history; Unitree Robotics' STAR Market IPO allocation rate hits a record low of 0.0181%, while some OTC dark pool intermediaries are bidding 520 yuan per share; Alibaba's Qwen Office platform has officially launched, debuting two major models: GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro; and Jensen Huang has partnered with six major Wall Street asset management giants to introduce a residual value guarantee mechanism for AI compute, establishing it as an independent asset class.
commentEn: Elon Musk snaps up Cursor, Anthropic races toward a $2 trillion valuation, and Unitree draws tens of thousands of applicants—the AI industry is shifting entirely from a tech race to a capital game, where whoever controls the tools, models, and hardware entry points will wield pricing power for the next decade.

newsItems.titleEn: SpaceX Officially Completes $60 Billion Acquisition of Cursor's Parent Company, Anysphere
newsItems.summaryEn: On August 14, SpaceX officially completed its $60 billion acquisition of Anysphere, the AI coding firm and parent company of Cursor. Founded just four years ago, Anysphere is now a wholly owned subsidiary of SpaceX. As Musk's largest AI acquisition to date, the deal marks a major shift in the AI coding tools landscape.

newsItems.titleEn: Anthropic Eyes October IPO at $2 Trillion Valuation, Potentially the Largest in History
newsItems.summaryEn: According to the Financial Times, leading global AI firm Anthropic could go public as early as October this year with an IPO valuation of $2 trillion, surpassing Elon Musk's SpaceX, which had a pre-IPO valuation of $1.77 trillion, to set a new record as the largest IPO in history.

newsItems.titleEn: Unitree Robotics IPO Allotment Rate Hits Record Low of 0.0181% on STAR Market, Grey Market Trading Red-Hot
newsItems.summaryEn: Unitree Robotics STAR Market IPO Results: 9.7846 million investors participated in the subscription, with the winning rate hitting a historic low of just 0.0181% on the STAR Market, while the subscription abandonment rate stood at a mere 0.09%. Meanwhile, OTC dark pool trading has quietly emerged, with some brokers bidding RMB 520 per share—a premium of over 2.4 times the RMB 150.8 issue price.

newsItems.titleEn: Qwen Office Debuts Two Frontier Models: GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro
newsItems.summaryEn: Alibaba's AI agent product, Qwen Office, has launched with GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro. Along with the previously released Qwen3.8-Max, Qwen Office now supports three cutting-edge models. Users can select these models directly from the product homepage, underscoring the intensifying competition among AI office agents.

newsItems.titleEn: Jensen Huang Joins Forces with Wall Street Giant to Launch AI Compute Residual Value Guarantees, Establishing a New Asset Class
newsItems.summaryEn: Jensen Huang has partnered with six Wall Street asset management giants to champion AI compute as a standalone asset class, with NVIDIA potentially providing a residual value support mechanism covering up to 25% of individual investment projects. Analysts view this as Huang putting tokenomics into practice, signaling that the AI boom is expanding from a technological race into a capital race, though it has also sparked investor concerns over circular financing.

titleEn: AI News | Chinese Doctor Cracks 22-Year Math Conjecture Using GPT-5.6 + Embodied AI Raises 93.5B in Six Months + Huaqiangbei AI Glasses Sales Double + DeepSeek Harness Architecture Overhaul + Major Google AI Talent Shakeup
summaryEn: Today's Top 5 AI Highlights: Dr. Jin Shanmu from Peking Union Medical College Hospital used GPT-5.6 to prove the Crouzeix Conjecture—a 22-year-old mathematical puzzle—in just 16 hours, pioneering AI-assisted mathematical proofs; the embodied AI sector continues to boom, with domestic funding in H1 2026 exceeding 93.5 billion yuan, a fivefold year-on-year increase; AI glasses sales in Huaqiangbei surged 100%, while sales across all AI product categories grew by 55%; the release of DeepSeek Harness has sparked architectural discussions, exploring AI's capacity for self-modification; and Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean steps down as DeepMind restructures, bringing turbulence to frontier AI R&D.
commentEn: AI is breaking through on two fronts simultaneously: upward, using mathematical proofs to reveal the ceiling of reasoning, and downward, permeating everyday life with smart glasses and robots—while Google's internal turmoil reminds us that the tech race is, at its core, a war for talent.

newsItems.titleEn: Chinese Doctor Cracks 22-Year-Old Math Problem Using GPT-5.6, Confirmed Correct by Crouzeix Himself
newsItems.summaryEn: Jin Shanmu, a postdoctoral fellow in neurosurgery at Peking Union Medical College Hospital, used OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol model to prove the Crouzeix conjecture—which has puzzled the mathematical community for 22 years since 2004—in just about 16 hours. Cornell mathematician Townsend and University of Washington Professor Greenbaum published a paper announcing this breakthrough, and Crouzeix himself has confirmed the proof's validity. This marks a milestone achievement for AI in the field of mathematical proof.

newsItems.titleEn: Over 93.5 Billion Yuan Pours into Embodied Intelligence Sector in H1 2026, Up 5-Fold YoY
newsItems.summaryEn: Robots are accelerating their entry into factory workforces, as investors pour substantial capital into the embodied AI sector. In the first half of 2026, total funding for China's embodied AI sector surpassed 93.5 billion yuan, marking a five-fold year-on-year increase. From factory logistics to manufacturing assembly lines, embodied AI is moving out of the lab and into real-world industrial settings, emerging as the next major battleground for AI deployment.

newsItems.titleEn: Huaqiangbei AI Glasses Sales Surge 100%; AI Product Sales Across All Categories Jump 55%
newsItems.summaryEn: In the first seven months of this year, sales across all AI product categories in Huaqiangbei grew by over 55% year-on-year. AI glasses sales surged by 100%, while drone and robot sales increased by 60% to 70%. Translation earbuds, 3D printing equipment, and smart wearables have become standout attractions for domestic and international visitors. Showcasing remarkable innovation speed, Huaqiangbei can design in the morning, prototype in the afternoon, begin mass production the next day, and ship products globally within a week, with its electronic exports now reaching over 190 countries worldwide.

newsItems.titleEn: DeepSeek Harness Architecture Innovation: Exploring Whether AI Can Modify Itself
newsItems.summaryEn: DeepSeek has launched the Harness architecture, abstracting models, tools, memory, skills, sessions, sandboxes, scheduling, and agent loops into a unified plugin system. The core bet lies not in the plugins themselves, but in exploring whether AI can modify its own capabilities. Grounded in the Cordis theoretical framework, Harness introduces reversible effects and dynamic composition mechanisms, offering a novel paradigm for AI agent architecture.

newsItems.titleEn: Massive Shake-Up in Google's AI Talent: Chief Scientist Jeff Dean Departs, DeepMind Restructured
newsItems.summaryEn: Google Faces Major AI Talent Shakeup. On August 5, Chief Scientist Jeff Dean announced his departure after 27 years at Google. That same day, parent company Alphabet announced a restructuring of DeepMind. A report by SemiAnalysis claims Google has abandoned frontier AI, while the Financial Times and Reuters reveal intense internal turmoil at DeepMind, with Demis Hassabis facing unprecedented internal pressure. Google's frontier AI R&D strategy is now at a major turning point.
